newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN IPOs - Rights issues fare poorly in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN IPOs - Rights issues fare poorly in 1996/97.

text.p: While mobilisation of funds through public issues of equity was poor in 1996/97 (April-March), rights issues fared much worse, according to a research firm.

Only 130 companies tapped the market for 272.4 billion rupees in 1996/97 against 291 issues for 652 billion the previous year, said Prithvi Haldea, managing director of Prime, the country's premier data base on the primary capital market.
The fall by amount mobilised is 58 percent while by number of issues, the decline is nearly 55 percent, he said in a report.
The poor state of the rights market did not augur well for industrial activity, the report said.
Both expansion and diversification programmes of several companies were affected, it said.
Haldea said a major reason for the continuing fall in rights issues was the poor state of the secondary capital market.
"Most rights issues are made at a premium and the offer price is, therefore, easily compared to the market price," he said. "The shortening gap between the two makes rights offers unattractive."
Several good issuers abstained from making rights issues as they did not want to offer prices significantly below the fundamentals, Haldea said.
Haldea said the boom in rights issues in 1992/93 and 1993/94 had also contributed to the present state of the rights market.
During these two years, a record 488 companies had offered rights issues aggregating 1,263 billion rupees, he said.
"However, as most of these issues led to subsequent losses at the investors' hands, the following years witnessed a continuing fall," the report said. Year No. of Rights Rights Issue

The report said the poor conditions in the secondary market not only kept most issuers away but also forced a lower premia on those issues which were made.
According to Prime, only 4 companies charged a premium above 100 rupees and only 16 companies above 50 rupese in 1996/97 against 16 and 41 the previous year.
Despite lower pricing, the response to issues was moderate and 29 percent of issues could not close on the scheduled closing dates, the report added.

Some of the bigger issues which faced poor response included ATN Entertainment, Parasrampuria Synthetics, Lloyd Electric & Engineering, Oscar Investments, Bhuwalka Steel Industries, Baroda Rayon, Patspin India, Malabar Trading, Progressive Commercial, VTC Industries and DCM Daewoo Motors, it said.
Further, the report said, poor or inetrvention by SEBI led to refund of application money by Ajcon Capital Markets, BCL Forgings, Kanoria Capital and Olympic Management.
As per Prime's report, 66 percent of the total amount raised in 1996/97 was through equity issued at a premium against 50 percent last year.
Rights issues by companies in the financial services sector accounted for nine percent of the total in 1996/97, down from 35 percent the previous year.
Prime said there were 50 issues above 100 million rupees against 111 last year and only four above one billion rupees against nine.
Haldea said given the present and projected poor state of the secondary market and investor apathy, the conditions are unlikley to improve much in 1997/98.
"with such poor prospects, several companies have deferred their rights issues indefinitely and are desperately looking for alternative sources of finance," he said.
